title: Ethiopian Spatchcock Chicken
community: Ethiopian modern kitchens — the flattened grilled chicken
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Spatchcock Grilled Chicken — a whole chicken butterflied, marinated in berbere and kibbeh for 4 hours, then grilled flat over charcoal until the berbere skin caramelises magnificently. The Ethiopian outdoor grill tradition applied to a whole chicken.
longDesc: Spatchcock berbere chicken combines two great cooking traditions — the Ethiopian berbere marinade and the charcoal grill. The flattened chicken cooks more evenly and faster, and the charcoal adds a smokiness that the oven cannot produce.
equipment: Kitchen scissors or knife for spatchcocking
steps: Remove backbone with scissors. Flatten chicken by pressing on breastbone.
Mix marinade. Score chicken deeply. Push marinade under skin and into all surfaces.
Grill over medium charcoal: 15—18 minutes per side.
Press with a heavy pan or foil-wrapped brick for the first 10 minutes.
Internal temperature must reach 74°C at the thickest point.
chefTips: The pressing weight is important — it ensures contact with the grill and even cooking.
Medium charcoal — berbere burns at high heat.
Spatchcocking halves the cooking time of a whole chicken.
cookingScience: Spatchcocking removes the thermal mass of the backbone cavity — the flattened chicken has a more uniform thickness, meaning all parts reach the safe internal temperature (74°C) at approximately the same time. This eliminates the common problem of overcooked breast and undercooked thigh.
healthBenefits: Charcoal grilling — less added fat than pan-cooking.
culturalNote: Ethiopian spatchcock berbere chicken is what the country's modern restaurants serve for outdoor celebrations — the charcoal grill, the berbere marinade, and the whole flattened chicken combine in a dish of pure theatrical impact.
